newsitem.title: USA: Federated seeks SEC probe about news report. [CORRECTED 21:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Federated seeks SEC probe about news report. [CORRECTED 21:54 GMT]

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc said on Tuesday that it has requested a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into a Business Week column that claimed that Federated offered to buy Mercantile Stores Co Inc.

Federated said there no present merger talks between Federated and Mercantile and Federated has made no such merger proposal. The Business Week article said Federated made a $75 a share offer to acquire Mercantile Stores.
Federated said in a statement that the news report "may have artificially depressed the market for Federated's stock."
Federated spokeswoman Carol Sanger said Federated had merger talks with Mercantile four years ago and has not had any talks since then.
Federated had later acquired Macy's in 1994.

Sanger questioned whether the source used in the article was attempting to manipulate the price of the stocks of at least one of the companies mentioned. (Corrects from "Sanger said the article was an attempt to manipulate the stock prices of at least one of the companies mentioned.")
Mercantile's shares surged almost ten percent on June 27 after the Business Week report was published. Mercantile's stock today is trading at 61-15/16, off 1 point.
Federated, a chain of 400 department stores and 150 specialty stores, said it does not ordinarily comment on market rumors.
Federated's shares gained 7/16 today, trading at 35-1/8, on 3.3 million shares of volume.
Mercantile was not immediately available for comment.
